core.metanarrative_position: Gospels: four canonical witnesses narrate Jesus with distinct literary emphases.

claims.statement: Luke says he investigated earlier material and wrote an orderly account so the reader may have certainty about what was taught.
John states that he selected signs so readers may believe Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life in His name.
The four canonical Gospels overlap substantially while arranging and emphasizing material differently.

core.interpretation_skill: Identify genre and context, separate direct observation from synthesis or inference, and connect the passage to the whole-Bible story without forced symbolism.

learning.foundation_objective: Explain in age-appropriate language that the Gospels are ancient narrative witnesses with distinct emphases and a shared claim about Jesus.
learning.extension_objective: Locate the lesson in the whole-Bible story and distinguish direct textual claims from later synthesis or application.

zero_prep_card.objective: Explain in age-appropriate language that the Gospels are ancient narrative witnesses with distinct emphases and a shared claim about Jesus.

say: Luke says he investigated earlier material and wrote an orderly account so the reader may have certainty about what was taught.

preparation.passage_context: Gospels: four canonical witnesses narrate Jesus with distinct literary emphases.
text_observations: Luke says he investigated earlier material and wrote an orderly account so the reader may have certainty about what was taught.
John states that he selected signs so readers may believe Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life in His name.
The four canonical Gospels overlap substantially while arranging and emphasizing material differently.
Distinct literary emphases do not by themselves amount to contradiction; alleged conflicts require passage-by-passage analysis.
interpretation_notes: Start with the principal passage before moving to supporting texts.
Keep genre and original audience visible.
Label synthesis, historical context, and application rather than presenting them as quotations.
theological_guardrails: Do not overclaim certainty about Gospel authorship, dating, sources, or harmonization where scholarship disputes details.
Do not solve every apparent difference by inventing events not supported by the text.
Distinguish theological purpose from fabrication; purposeful selection is explicit in John.

likely_questions.question: Why are some events in one Gospel but not another?
likely_questions.purpose: Ancient authors selected and arranged material according to purpose; John explicitly says not everything Jesus did was included.

likely_questions.question: Do differences mean contradictions?
likely_questions.purpose: Not automatically. Each alleged conflict must be examined carefully rather than assumed either way.

accessibility.plain_language_rule: Prefer short sentences, define unfamiliar biblical terms, and do not require independent reading beyond the segment.

Allow verbal, written, or pointing responses.
Preview transitions and allow a pass option.
sensory_notes: No activity requires loud sound, forced touch, or competitive speed.
non_reader_support: Teacher or parent may read aloud.
Use sequence cards, symbols, or oral responses.

do_not_ask: Do not require disclosure of private family circumstances.
Do not require public confession or religious decision.
Do not use physical touch without consent.
safeguarding.teacher_response: If a child discloses harm, danger, abuse, severe distress, or unmet basic needs, follow the congregation safeguarding process rather than trying to investigate in class.
